This complaint is filed under Sec. 200 of Cr. P. C. for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

2. It is the case of the complainant that:
The complainant and accused are known to each other since several years.
The accused was running chit business since few years.
She offerred the complainant to invest money in the chit business of sum of Rs. Rs.5,00,000/- for a period of 31 months on monthly chit amount of Rs.13,000/-.
The complainant paid up to 28 th chit and chit was closed on 04-01-2024.
After completing the chit period, the accused has to pay to the complainant a sum of Rs.4,75,000/-.

At that time the accused has issued post dated cheque bearing No.18619 for Rs.2,75,000/- dated 25-05-2024 drawn on Canara Bank, Bangalore Institute of Technology, Bangalore and promised to pay the balance amount of Rs.2,01,000/- by way of cash.

3. As per the instructions of the accused, the complainant presented the cheque through her banker Canara Bank, Girinagar Branch, Bengaluru, but the said cheque was returned with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient" dated 04-07-2024.
The complainant issued legal notice to the accused on 23-07-2024 through RPAD.
In spite of service of notice, the accused has not paid the cheque amount.

Accordingly, the accused has committed an offence punishable under Sec.138 of N.I Act,
hence, the complaint.
4. After recording the sworn statement of the complainant and verifying the documents, cognizance was taken against the accused for the offence punishable under Sec. 138 of N.I. Act.
The accused on receiving the summons appeared before this Court through her counsel, she was enlarged on bail and her plea was recorded.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
Hence, the case was posted for arguments.
5. The complainant got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to 9 and Ex.P13 to Ex.P14.
During the cross-examination of DW.1 the learned counsel for the complainant has confronted the documents and got marked as Ex.P10 to Ex.P12.
Then, the case was posted for recording the statement of accused under Sec.313 Cr.P.C.

In the statement U/s 313 Cr.P.C., the Suma vs Mamatha S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173732117/
2 accused has denied all the incriminating evidence appearing against her and claimed to be tried.
The accused got examined herself as DW.1.
Hence, the case was posted for argument.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
7.

The following points arise for my consideration:
1.
Whether the complainant proves that accused has committed offence punishable under Sec.138 of N.I. Act?
2. What order?

8. My findings on the above points are as under Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: As per final order for the following:
-: R E A S O N S :-
9. POINT NO.1:-

It is the definite case of the complainant that, towards the discharge of the legally recoverable debt, accused has issued disputed cheque in favour of the complainant and when the cheque was presented, same was dishonoured for the reason "Funds Insufficient".
Though the said fact was brought to the notice of the accused by issuing legal notice, but accused has failed to repay the cheque amount.
10. In order to substantiate the contention, the complainant got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked in all 9 documents as ExP1 to Ex.P14.
If the documents produced by the complainant are perused, Ex.P1 is the cheque which bears the signature alleged to be of the accused.
The accused nowhere has disputed the cheque which relates to her account and she even has not disputed her signature in the Ex.P1.
It is deposed by Pw1 that cheque in question was issued by the accused towards the discharge of legal liability.
Deposit slip is marked at Ex.P2.
The cheque in question was presented by the complainant through her banker which was returned with memo as per ExP3 stating 'Funds Insufficient".
Hence, she got issued legal notice to the accused through RPAD, which is produced at Ex.P.4.
The postal receipts are marked at Ex.P.5 and Ex.P6.
The Postal acknowledgment is marked at Ex.P7.
Track consignment is marked at Ex.P8.
Certified copy of FIR with compliant is marked at Ex.P9.
Certified copy of compliant in CC No. 14913/2024 is marked at Ex.P10.
Certified copy of compliant and written statement in OS NO.8017/2024 is marked at Ex.P11 and Ex.P12.
Certified copy of whats App conversation held between the daughter of the complainant with the accused is marked at Ex.P13.

PEN drive is marked at Ex.P13(a) and Certificate u/Sec. 63 (4)
BSA of 2023 is marked at Ex.P14.
11.

The accused while admitting that complainant is known to her has taken the defence that one Balaji the resident of Girinagar was running chit business in which complainant, accused and six to seven others were the members.
The said Balaji did not pay the chit amount to the members including the accused.

Though the accused tried to contact Balaji with regard to the payment of chit Suma vs Mamatha S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173732117/
3 amount, but he did not available for contact.
Hence, the complainant and Ashalath, accusing that accused herself was running the chit business and accused did not return the chit amount had lodged false complaint.
It is because Balaji is known person to the accused and that accused is a working women and earning income, in order to extract money from the accused, they have lodged false police complaint.

It is the further case of the accused that even though Balaji was ready to issue his cheque towards the chit amount but the complainant insisted the accused to give her cheque and that even though Balaji had paid the chit amount to the complainant but complainant has not returned the cheque of the accused and complainant collected the cheque forcibly from the accused at the police station and that no transaction of any nature was held between her and the complainant, hence she is not liable to pay the cheque amount.
12.

In order to substantiate the defence, the accused got examined herself as DW.1.
13.

If the entire materials placed on record is perused, accused has not disputed the financial capacity of the complainant to invest money in the alleged chit business and has not disputed the service of legal notice to her.
Hence, discussion on the above said two point does not warrant.
It is further relevant to state here that accused has not disputed the cheque in question relates to her account so also her signature in the disputed cheque.

Hence, as held in catena of decisions of Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court benefit of presumption raises in favour of the complainant u/Sec. 118 and 139 of NI Act regarding issuance of cheque towards the discharge of legally enforceable debt.
Now it is for the accused to rebut the presumption with preponderance of probabilities.

14. It was much argued by the learned defence counsel that complainant has not proved the chit business and has not proved the amount invested by her in the chit business by not examining any of the members of the chit business.

By referring the evidence of complainant wherein she has stated about the complaint lodged by her against the accused for not returning the chit amount and thereby defrauded the complainant, it was argued by the learned defence counsel that Ex.P9 (ie) FIR and complaint is the complaint lodged by one Ashalatha but not by the complainant and that there is no reference of the name of complainant in the Ex.P9 hence Ex.P9 would no way helpful to the case of the complainant.

The learned defence counsel in further has argued that though the complainant has referred about Srikar Group by relying upon Ex.P13 but she is not in a position to state who that person named "Srikar" and that in the Ex.P13 there is no mention of the name of complainant or of amount transferred by her towards the chit business and there is no mention of the cheque in question issued by the accused towards the said chit business and that there is no evidence as to in whose mobile, the screen short of the Whats App conversation was taken.
Hence submitted that the case of the complaint is laid on the foundation of falsehood.

15. In the light of the defence taken by the accused and the line of argument canvassed by the learned defence counsel if the materials placed on record is perused, admittedly accused is a law graduate working in the legal Department at Vokkaligara Sangha Trust as legal Assistance.
Hence, it can be said that accused is well qualified lady having legal knowledge.
From the evidence of complainant it can be gathered that she is an illiterate lady.
She do not know how to operate Whats App and she do not even have Whats App in her mobile.

The PW.1 has deposed that her daughter Suma vs Mamatha S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173732117/
4 who is an Engineer was operating Whats App and was conversating with the accused on behalf of complainant towards the chit business.
To evidence the said fact the complainant has produced Ex.P13 (ie.,) Screen shot of Whats App conversation.
It is not in dispute that the name of the daughter of complainant is Shruthi and the mobile number of the accused is 9886614948.
If Ex.P13 is carefully perused, Whats App group under the name "Srikar Group" was created, in which accused was the group Admin.
In the Ex.P13 we can find the name of Shruthi with DP in which we can see the picture of complainant with her daughter.
It is true that in the Ex.P13 we can see several mobile numbers and PW.1 had pleaded ignorance as to whose mobile number all those are.
It is not necessary that merely because complainant is the member of Srikar group she must know the mobile number of all the members of Srikar Group.
Further the name "Srikar" is given to that particular whats App group.
It is not necessary that by referring any particular person the group under the name Srikar group was created.
Hence, it is not the worth argument canvased by the learned defence counsel that complainant is not knowing who that person called "Srikar".
It is the name of the Whats App group created by the accused but not the name of any person so as to identify that person by the complainant.

16. At the risk of repetition it is the defence of the accused that she had no chit transaction with the complainant or any other person and that one Balaji had chit business with complainant, accused and others and that at the initial stage Balaji had failed to pay the subscribed chit amount to the members.

Since Balaji is known to the accused, even though Balaji was ready to issue his cheque towards security for the payment of subscribed chit amount but complainant insisted the accused to issue her cheque as security towards the amount payable by Balaji and that even though Balaji had paid entire amount to the chit members but complainant failed to return the cheque issued by the accused towards security.
17. As stated supra, the accused at first has disputed her having chit transaction with the complainant and others.
But in order to evidence the chit transaction which the accused had with the complainant and Ors., the complainant has relied upon Ex.P9 to Ex.P13 and the oral evidence of the accused.

If the oral evidence is perused, during the cross examination of PW.1, the learned defence counsel themselves had posed suggestion that "only the complainant and 3 others had invested money with the accused in the chit business".
By posing suggestion to the aforesaid effect the accused has admitted her running chit business in which complainant was one of the member.

Apart from the very admission of the accused of her running chit business, in order to prove the said point, the complainant has relied upon Ex.P9 to Ex.P13.
18.

Ex.P9 is the complaint lodged by one Ashalatha against the accused and Ors on 10-07-2024 alleging that accused who is running chit business having taken chit amount from Ashalatha and several others failed to pay the amulgamated chit amount and when Ashalatha demanded the accused to repay the chit amount, at that time accused and others have abused and given criminal intimidation to her.

19. If the averments of the complaint and FIR at Ex.P9 is read in whole, wherein the name of Suma the complainant herein is referred as one of the victim of the crime under the hands of accused herein as accused has cheated even the complainant herein by not retuning the chit amount to the Suma vs Mamatha S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173732117/
5 tune of Rs.4,76,000/-.
It is true that complainant has not produced any document to prove that she had lodged separate complaint against the accused before Bytarayanapura police station.

The PW.1 has clearly deposed that she had also been to Bytarayanapura police station to lodge the complaint against the accused and she had also lodged complainant but the Station House Officer informed her it would not possible to register separate FIR against the accused on the complainant of all the victims of the offence and they would register one FIR on the basis of the complaint of all the victims.
The very mention of the name of complainant herein, name of Saroja and Ors in the FIR at Ex.P9 justifies the evidence given by the PW.1 to the aforesaid effect.

20. Further Ex.P11is the suit for recovery of money filed by Ashalatha in OS No.8017/2024 on the file of City Civil Court Bangalore against the accused herein wherein also the plaintiff therein has taken the contention of chit business run by the accused and the money collected by the accused towards chit investment and failure on the part of the accused to return the invested chit amount to the subscribers.

21. If Ex.P13 is perused, it clearly discloses that accused was running chit business, she had created Whats App group under the name Srikar Group and in Ex.P13 there is mention about collection of chit amount from several persons till 29th chit.
Even it is the case of complainant that she had paid up to 29 th chit of the amount of Rs.13,000/- each.
Hence, the oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence clearly proves the chit business run by the accused and the amount invested upto 29th chit by the complainant.

When accused herself had posed suggestion to the PW.1 that PW.1 was the member in the chit business of the accused, under such circumstances, further proof for chit business run by the accused by examining the members of the chit business and the daughter of the complainant would not require.
As provided under section 58 of the Evidence Act Admitted facts need not be proved.

22. So far as the defence taken by the accused regarding Balaji running the chit business in which complainant and accused were the members and the cheque issued by the accused towards the chit amount due by Balaji as security is concerned, if accused is no way related to the said chit business,
question of her issuing cheque towards security does not arise and the question of complainant insisting the accused to issue her cheque towards the chit transaction of Balaji does not arise .
If really Balaji was due of the chit amount then complainant would have insisted or demanded Balaji to issue his cheque and there was no necessity for the accused to issue her cheque.

So far as the defence taken by the accused in her evidence in chief is concerned, if the entire cross examination of PW.1 is perused, no where the accused has posed any suggestion to the PW.1 regarding the amount invested by the complainant in the chit business of Balaji and the chit amount due by Balaji and the cheque in question given by the accused as the security for the chit amount due by Balaji etc., Mere taking defence in the evidence would not suffice.
The defence taken by the accused has to be put in the cross examination of PW.1.
Hence, what ever the defence taken by the accused in her evidence has no legal sanctity when such defence taken by her has not been questioned to the PW.1.

What ever the defence taken by the accused in his evidence is by surprise without bringing such defence to the notice of the complainant either by stating the said defence in the reply notice or while cross examination of PW.1.
Further in order to prove the said defence, the accused ought to have examined Balaji as witness.

Hence, withholding of material witness adverse inference can be drawn Suma vs Mamatha S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173732117/
6 against the case of the accused.
The accused having not denied the service of notice not given any explanation for her not giving reply to the notice.
If the defence taken by the accused is true and real then nothing prevented the accused from giving reply notice and to take the defence at the first instance in the reply notice.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment reported in 2025 (4) KCCR 3277 between P Karnataka Gandhi Vs. Raju Rao wherein also the accused having served the legal notice not chosen to send any reply to the said notice putting forth his defence at the earliest.

sentences.text: Hence among other grounds on the ground of not giving reply notice the Honble High Court set aside the order of Acquittal.
23. 2025 (4) KCCR 3452 between N M Rajashekariah Vs. A.D Girijamma.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also cheque issued by accused was dishonoured and legal notice duly served were unanswered.
Accused admitted signature on cheque.
No credible evidence was produced to support allegation of misuse of signed cheque.
Under the given set of facts accused was convicted for the offence u/Sec.138 of NI Act.
24 . It is opt to state here that accused has taken the defence that her cheque was forcibly taken on May 2024 at Bytarayanapura Police station.
If complaint at Ex.P9 is perused, it was lodged on 10-07-2024.
It is the only one criminal case that was lodged before Bytarayanapura police station u/Sec. 504, 506 and 420 IPC.

Hence when complaint as per Ex.P9 was lodged on 10-07-2024, the question of taking the cheque of accused in the month of May -2024 at Bytarayanapura police station does not arise because in the mouth of May -2024 no complaint was lodged against accused at Bytarayanapura police station so as to accused appear before Bytarayanapura police and to get her cheque out of threat or coercion.

Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of discussion that in the month of May -2024 the accused was forced to give her cheque, then when the accused being law graduate working as Legal Assistant could have taken legal action against the complainant.
But no such steps against complainant was taken so far.
Further being well educated having graduation in law accused would not have heeded to the alleged unlawful demand to issue her cheque.
Further if the statement given by accused u/Sec. 313 Cr.PC is perused, wherein the accused has stated that she has repaid entire amount by way of cash and online transfer.

In the statement u/Sec. 313 Cr.PC,
the accused nowhere has referred the name of Balaji and nowhere has stated that she had given her cheque as security.
Further if really accused had no transaction with the complainant question of her paying the amount as stated in her 313 statement by way of cash and online transfer would not arise.
If really accused had paid the chit amount by way of online she could have proved the same by producing her Bank statement.
Hence, it can be said that the accused has taken all together three contradictory defence one in her statement u/Sec. 313 Cr.PC, one in the cross examination of PW.1 and one in the defence evidence.

25. On appreciating the entire materials placed on record it can be said that the complainant has complied all the statutory requirement and complainant has proved that the accused has committed offence u/Sec. 138 of the NI Act.
Accused has miserably failed to rebut the presumption by not proving the defence with preponderance of probabilities.
Accordingly, I answered Point No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: POINT No.2 :- The Negotiable Instruments Act is a Special Enactment, and the provisions of the Act prevail over the general provisions contained in Code of Criminal Procedure.
Therefore, keeping the relevant provisions of the Act in mind the sentence is to be passed.

In the light of the reasons on the Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER  Acting under Sec. 278(2) of BNSS the  accused is found guilty of the offence punishable under section 138 read with section 142 of NI Act.

Consequently, accused is sentenced to pay fine of Rs.2,85,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Eighty Five Thousand only), out of which Rs.2,80,000/- shall be paid as compensation to the complainant under Sec.396 of BNSS and Rs.5,000/- shall be payable to the State.
In the event of default in payment within a period of one month, the accused shall be convicted to simple imprisonment for a period of 4 months.
It is made clear that in view of Sec.430 of BNSS, even if the accused under goes the default sentence imposed above, she is not absolved of liability to pay the fine amount.
The bail bond of accused and that of surety stands canceled.
Office to furnish the copy of this judgment free of cost to the accused.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 1st day of April 2026.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl.SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
